newsitem.title: RUSSIA: "State of the Nation? Terrible," Yeltsin says.
newsitem.headline: "State of the Nation? Terrible," Yeltsin says.

text.p: The following is a selection of quotations from President Boris Yeltsin's annual state of the nation address to be published on Thursday.
The 66-page text will be presented to legislators at a joint session of the two houses of parliament on Thursday and form the basis of a keynote policy speech by Yeltsin.
ON THE STATE OF THE NATION
"Most Russians are unhappy with today and scared of tomorrow...People's patience has run out."

"Russia entered 1997 with a heavy load of problems. More than half its citizens are suffering from delays in wage and pension payments; the stranglehold of non-payment is paralysing the economy and the state apparatus is being corroded by corruption; the authorities scarcely manage to put laws and decrees into effect. And this is just one small part of our unresolved problems."
ON RESTORING ORDER
"Russia needs order. But there are two difficult questions to answer: what kind of order and how to impose it?"
"Order in the country will emerge only together with the order in the state apparatus itself."
"Power unlimited by law is dangerous while law not backed by power is impotent...Our choice is order based on law."
ON ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL REFORM

"An effective market economy is not just freedom for private enterprise but also a strict legal order -- common, stable and generally observed rules of economic activity. The task of the state is to set such rules and to make sure they are obeyed."
"The main obstacle to establishing a new economic order and the new political system is the inefficiency of the authorities and disorder within the state apparatus"

"In 1992, Russia had only one way to save its economy from collapse -- to put its faith in the power of economic freedom. (But) market relations have established themselves in sectors where they should be taboo. When free buying and selling extends to the passing of laws, to the work of civil servants and to court decisions, it is not just immoral but a mortal danger to society and the state."
ON FIGHTING CRIME AND CORRUPTION
"We have declared war on the economic crime and corruption but have not started it for real."

"The problem of economic crime and corruption has grown from what was clearly a police matter, as it is in most countries, into a political issue. The criminal world has openly challenged the state and launched into open competition with it."
"To fight economic crime and corruption effectively we need to expose those who initiate and organise crimes, the so-called godfathers, rather than just those who merely carry them out."
ON PROSPECTS FOR POLITICAL STABILITY

"Most politicians soberly consider the mood of the voters and do not try to link solving any single issue with changing the whole social, political and economic system. Radicalism is losing ground in the Russian society."
"There is a real chance to switch from implacable political struggle to normal political life, from conflict to cooperation."
ON THE ARMED FORCES
"Russia's armed forces are five to 10 years, sometimes up to 15 years behind the world's most powerful armies in the general level of techical equipment."
ON FOREIGN POLICY

"Times are getting critical for Europe. Let me remind you: without Russia, and even more so against her, no one in Europe has yet been able and will ever be able to create an effective system of security."
"The most important direction for our state policy in 1997 will be Russian-Belarussian integration. This year will be a year of great new decisions for Russia and Belarus."
